stories.headline: A river otter is back on California's San Mateo coast
stories.summary: An amateur naturalist's trail cameras on a 5,100-acre preserve caught a river otter 3 times, the first documented on that coast since the 1800s fur trade wiped them out.
stories.why: Cleaner creeks and protected land are letting otters return to places they vanished from.

stories.headline: A 150-million-year-old bird had dinosaur teeth and couldn't fly
stories.summary: The crow-sized Yuezhuornis had serrated teeth, a sickle-shaped toe claw and legs built for the ground. It's the earliest known bird lineage to lose the ability to fly.
stories.why: Early birds weren't all racing to fly better: some gave flying up almost from the start.

stories.headline: Satellites now tell rangers which wild toilets need a visit
stories.summary: New Zealand put 50+ satellite-linked sensors at 20+ remote huts and toilets, so crews only fly in when needed, cutting helicopter trips and about 30 tonnes of CO2.
stories.why: The same network could soon check predator traps, helping protect native birds from rats and stoats.

stories.headline: Half a million strangers flood bullied people with kindness
stories.summary: The Kindness Mob picks someone facing a wave of online hate and buries the trolls in compliments. Since 2023 it has helped about 400 people, like a woman mocked for a weight-loss video.
stories.why: They try never to let the person find out. The only goal is to make the internet feel kind.

fun_fact: River otters can live 8 to 15 years in the wild, and a female can have up to 6 pups in a litter.
